title: The Script Rome Conquered That Became Arabic 🤯
script: A conquered people used their conqueror's alphabet — to erase them from history. The Nabataeans of Petra absorbed Rome's Aramaic script in the 1st century BC, then twisted it so completely it became modern Arabic — spoken today by 400 million people. But here's the wild part: Rome had no idea. In 106 AD, Roman legions marched into Petra convinced they'd won. They had no clue the Nabataeans had already rewritten the future of human language. Send this to someone who still thinks Rome controlled everything it touched.
search_summary: Nabataeans of Petra transformed Rome's Aramaic script into the Arabic alphabet, spoken by 400 million people today.
comment_question: Did Rome actually conquer Petra, or did Petra conquer Rome's legacy? 🤯

title: The Fish That Snipes Insects from Underwater 😱
script: This animal knocks prey out of the air — without jumping, without flying, with sniper-level accuracy. The archerfish fires a jet of water up to 3 meters, corrects for the way light bends between water and air, and almost never misses. But here's the wild part — it gets better by watching other archerfish shoot. Not instinct. Pure observation. Send this to someone who still thinks copying to learn is a human thing.
search_summary: Archerfish shoots water jets up to 3 meters to knock insects out of the air with sniper accuracy and learns by watching others.
comment_question: If a fish can learn by watching others, what's your excuse? 👀
